topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture’s relationship to earlier teaching and sets out its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains cancer evolution through successive mutations that give expanding cell clones a selective advantage.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption as a route to tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines whether altered transcriptional accessibility can initiate tumors without genetic mutations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and the cancer stem cell model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell’s position in a tissue hierarchy and its capacity for self-renewal influence tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness in cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that allow previously nonmalignant mutant cells to form tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains established tumors’ dependence on supportive surrounding cells and the therapeutic opportunities arising from that dependence.

topics.label: Studying and synthesizing cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop an evidence-based understanding of cancer evolution as the emergence of malignant clones through interactions between cellular properties and a permissive environment.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces cancer therapy as the subject of the next session.
